obligation: FSIS notification of adulterated or misbranded product in commerce
trigger: The establishment learns or determines, or has reason to believe, that adulterated or misbranded meat product received by or originating from it has entered commerce (for example, product shipped after an unapproved cook cycle change, with a wrong label or missing allergen statement, or after unmonitored cold storage, and evaluation finds it adulterated or misbranded)
deadline: Within 24 hours of learning or determining; include the type, amount, origin, and destination of the product
notify: Local FSIS District Office; then follow the written recall procedure (9 CFR 418.3)

trigger: Responsible party determines an article of food is a reportable food
deadline: No later than 24 hours after the determination
applies_at_this_tier: No - the responsible party is the FDA registrant (350f(a)(1)); the plant is regulated exclusively by USDA and does not register (21 CFR 1.226(g)). FSIS notice under 9 CFR 418.2 applies instead

trigger: Breach of security of personal information of Florida residents (here, employee data in the suite, on the office desktop, or at the payroll service). Clock starts at determination of the breach or reason to believe one occurred
deadline: No later than 30 days after determination (a 15-day extension is possible for good cause under 501.171(3)(a), for notice to individuals only)
notify: Affected Florida residents (current and former employees)
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - if employee personal information was accessed or acquired

obligation: Florida notice to the Department of Legal Affairs
trigger: Breach affecting 500 or more individuals in Florida
deadline: No later than 30 days after determination; the 15-day good-cause extension does not apply to this notice
notify: Florida Department of Legal Affairs (Attorney General)
applies_at_this_tier: Unlikely - about 30 current and former employees' records are held; applies only if 500 or more Floridians are affected

obligation: Florida notice to consumer reporting agencies
trigger: Notice required to more than 1,000 individuals at a single time
A law enforcement agency determines individual notice would interfere with a criminal investigation
deadline: Delay on the agency's written request for the period it specifies
notify: Hold Florida individual notices; keep the written request

obligation: Florida third-party agent notice to the company (inbound)
trigger: Breach of a system maintained by a third-party agent for the company (payroll service, MSP, backup vendor)
deadline: As expeditiously as practicable and no later than 10 days after the agent's determination

trigger: Affected former employees who now live outside Florida
notify: Residents and regulators under each state's law

obligation: OFAC sanctions check before any ransom payment
citation: OFAC Updated Advisory on Potential Sanctions Risks for Facilitating Ransomware Payments (Sept. 21, 2021); 31 CFR ch. V
deadline: Before any payment; full and timely reporting to law enforcement or CISA is a mitigating factor
notify: OFAC (license if a sanctioned party is involved); FBI through IC3 or CISA

obligation: Voluntary report to FBI and CISA
trigger: Ransomware or other significant cyber incident
deadline: As soon as practicable (Day 0 to Day 2 in the runbook)
notify: FBI field office or IC3; CISA

trigger: Suspected security incident, extortion demand, or data theft
deadline: Per policy: prompt notice through the 24x7 breach hotline, before hiring outside firms; use panel counsel and forensics

obligation: MSP incident notice to the company (inbound)
trigger: Security incident affecting the MSP's tools or the company's systems
deadline: None in the current contract; 24 hours to be added at renewal (P01 R-012)

obligation: Customer notice (regional grocery chain and wholesale accounts)
trigger: Incident affecting product safety, a recall, delivery, or customer data
deadline: Per each agreement; the grocery chain's supplier agreement asks for prompt notice of any recall or food safety event
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - contractual, not legal; Office Manager keeps the list

obligation: CIRCIA covered cyber incident report / ransom payment report (PROPOSED - not yet in effect)
trigger: Covered cyber incident or ransom payment
deadline: Proposed: 72 hours after reasonable belief a covered cyber incident occurred; 24 hours after a ransom payment
applies_at_this_tier: No - final rule not published as of 2026-09-25; as proposed the company is far below the size criterion (7 employees against a 1,000-employee SBA standard). Recheck when final

obligation: Reporting of actual or threatened cyber incidents at MTSA facilities / OCS facilities / vessels
trigger: Cyber incident at an MTSA-regulated facility
notify: FBI, CISA, and the Coast Guard Captain of the Port; or National Response Center
applies_at_this_tier: No - the plant is not an MTSA-regulated facility

trigger: Contractor identifies covered equipment or a Kaspersky covered article
deadline: Within 1 business day of identification for covered telecommunications equipment or services (52.204-25(d)); within 3 business days for a Kaspersky covered article (52.204-23(c)); further report within 10 business days in both cases
applies_at_this_tier: No - the company holds no federal contracts
